title: A rival middleman arrives
hook: A middleman keeps $1. A rival middleman arrives. Do they split the dollar?

knows: a middleman buys low and sells high
doesNotKnow: that once a second trader can reach the seller, competition bids the price up to the buyer's value and the traders earn nothing

misconception: Adding a second middleman just splits the middleman's profit in two.
objective: The learner can explain that because each trader can resell for $1, each prefers outbidding by a cent to losing the item, so the bid rises to $1: the seller gets the whole $1 and the traders earn nothing.

claims.text: With one trader linked to the seller ($0) and a buyer ($1), the trader can bid $0 and sell for $1, keeping the whole $1.
claims.source: Model rule: the seller has no other buyer and the buyer no other seller. Demo.tsx monopoly state (seller 0, T1 1, buyer 0). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Monopoly state in Demo.tsx: bid 0, T1 keeps 1 - 0 = $1; follows from the model rules.

claims.text: With two traders able to buy from the seller, each with her own $1 buyer, each prefers outbidding by a cent to losing the item, so the bid climbs to $1.00, where bidding more would lose money: the seller takes the whole $1 and the traders keep $0; a second trader does not halve the profit, it goes to the seller.
claims.source: Alternating 1-cent best responses from $0: 100 outbids to $1.00, trader profit 1 - 1 = 0. Demo.tsx go(); re-run in node (ncm-e00); matches the brief's check. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node of alternating 1-cent outbids: 100 outbids, bid $1.00 (T1 leads, even), profit 0, seller $1. Note for the builder (non-blocking): the last outbid, $0.99 to $1.00, is a tie (0 either way), so 'would rather outbid' is weak preference there; the limit result is standard Bertrand competition.

claims.text: The lesson simplifies the trading-network model of Blume, Easley, Kleinberg and Tardos.
claims.source: Blume, Easley, Kleinberg and Tardos, 'Trading networks with price-setting agents', Games and Economic Behavior 67(1), 2009; Easley and Kleinberg 2010, ch. 11. Fact-checker to confirm. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): BEKT, 'Trading networks with price-setting agents', Games Econ. claims.text: The lesson is a simplified model: each trader resells to her own buyer for the buyer's full $1, bids move a cent at a time, T1 bids first.
claims.source: Assumptions of Demo.tsx; stage chip 'Model: each trader resells to her own $1 buyer' and the reveal's last line. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Matches the stage chip and the reveal's muted line; Demo.tsx go() and leader rule.

recall.question: An artist values a sketch at $0. Two dealers can each buy it, and each has her own collector who will pay $500. What does the artist end up getting?
recall.why: Each dealer can resell for $500, so each outbids the other until the bid reaches $500 and neither keeps a profit.
